about: Held-out canonical retrieval set: one founder's evolving company state (46 chat statements in time order, then 82 labelled questions). Written 2026-10-17 BEFORE the canonical relevance-gate change was implemented, and frozen (FROZEN.sha256 next to this file) before its first run. It exists because retrieval-core.v1 has been tuned against for weeks and is development data. Covers current vs superseded values, explicit corrections, a compound change, negation, cancellation, a hedged plan, two projects (Brightloop, Atlas), two people sharing a first name, a competitor's price as a distractor, paraphrases with no shared words, and 26 questions that must get NO context (unknown personal facts, general knowledge, questions addressed to the assistant, and known entities asked about an unknown attribute).
limitations: Same author as the change it evaluates (an AI engineer who had read retrieval-core.v1's failures); written before the change and frozen before its first run, but not author-independent.
Synthetic, single persona, single conversation; 82 questions. Differences of a few queries are noise.
Labels judge retrieval (which statements should reach the answer model), not answers.
`stale` lists statements that a CURRENT question must not receive as current; superseded claims shown on a past-tense question are labelled 'no longer current' by the renderer and are not counted.

corpus.statement: I'm Maya, the founder and CEO of Brightloop.
Brightloop makes scheduling software for physiotherapy clinics.
We're based in Lisbon.
Our price is $29 per clinic per month.
We're planning to launch publicly on April 14.
Tomás is our CTO.
Ines leads design at Brightloop.
Our biggest blocker is the Google Calendar sync, which keeps dropping appointments.
Lena Brandt from Northwind Ventures is our lead investor.
We have 42 paying clinics.
Atlas is my side project, an analytics dashboard for running clubs.
The Atlas beta is due at the end of March.
Kofi is helping me build Atlas on weekends.
We use Stripe for billing.
Our backend is written in Elixir.
We decided not to build an Android app this year.
Our monthly burn is about $38k.
Our runway is 14 months.
I usually take investor calls on Fridays.
The mobile release is planned for May 15.
We're planning a team offsite in Porto in June.
Tomás owns the calendar sync integration.
Our main competitor is ClinicFlow.
ClinicFlow charges $49 per month.
Sam Ortiz is our accountant.
Sam Lee joined as a backend engineer.
Sam Lee reports to Tomás.
Northwind wants a board update every quarter.
The next board meeting is on July 8.
Our goal is to reach 100 paying clinics by December.
I studied sports science before starting Brightloop.
We're thinking about adding patient reminders, but nothing is decided.
We moved the public launch to May 2 because of the sync bug.
We raised our price to $39 per clinic per month.
Rui has taken over design from Ines.
The Google Calendar sync is fixed now.
Our biggest blocker now is getting the data processing agreement signed with our hosting provider.
We're now at 57 paying clinics.
We cancelled the Porto offsite.
Kofi is no longer working on Atlas.
We pushed the mobile release to June 20 and hired Wren as our first support lead.
Wren will handle onboarding calls for new clinics.
Correction: our runway is 11 months, not 14.
The Atlas beta slipped to April 20.
Our churn last month was 3%.
The investor update is due next Monday.
